title: Each Primitive Invocation records three workflow stages: initial planning, Operational GovOps Review, and Artifact Edit Proposal
content:
Every Instance Configuration Document in the Osero Artifact carries a Data Repository with exactly three children, in the same order. A.6.1.1.7.2.1.1.3.1.3.1 holds "the materials associated with initial planning of the Invocation of this Instance"; .3.2 holds "the materials associated with Operational GovOps Review during the Invocation"; .3.3 holds "the materials associated with preparing the Artifact Edit Proposal during the Invocation."

Read as a sequence, this exposes the standard path by which anything an Agent does becomes part of the Atlas: someone plans the Invocation, GovOps reviews it operationally, and the result is written up as a proposed edit to the Artifact. The Artifact is therefore not a description maintained alongside operations — it is the terminus of the operational process.

The placement of the review stage is the informative part. GovOps review happens *during* the Invocation, before the Artifact Edit Proposal is prepared, so operational objections are raised while the action is still being shaped rather than at the point of a governance vote on final text.

Because these three folders exist on every Instance regardless of Primitive, the workflow is not something each Agent designs; it is imposed by the document structure, and an Invocation with an empty review folder is visibly incomplete.
description: The per-Instance Data Repository fixes the route any Primitive use takes into the Atlas — plan, then an operations review, then a proposal to edit the Artifact text itself.
